chapters.title: Chapter 11: Project: PocketCFO App, Part 1
chapters.goal: Build the first version of a JavaFX personal finance application with layered domain, repository, service, and view classes, then add update and delete behavior.

exercises.title: Build the PocketCFO Application
exercises.description: Create the first JavaFX version of PocketCFO for transactions, categories, savings goals, obligations, and monthly summaries.

explanation.summary: The transaction domain class captures one income or expense entry with its identity, date, category, amount, and description.

lines.text: The identifier stays fixed for the lifetime of a transaction, allowing repository operations to find the correct entry later.

lines.code: public Transaction(long id, LocalDate date, TransactionType type, String categoryName,
lines.text: The constructor requires every value needed to create a complete transaction rather than leaving partially initialized objects.
Money uses BigDecimal so calculations do not inherit the rounding surprises of binary floating-point values.

explanation.run: Use the guided replay to materialize and test the PocketCFO project.

phases: Create the Maven and JavaFX project plus transaction entry.
Add category targets, totals, and over-budget warnings.
Add savings goals and leftover allocation.
Add recurring obligations and monthly equivalents.
Wire the complete monthly summary and verify the project.

exercises.title: Add Update and Delete Operations
exercises.description: Extend PocketCFO repositories and views so categories, transactions, savings goals, and obligations can be corrected or removed.

explanation.summary: The repository replaces the transaction with the matching id and then persists the revised collection.

lines.text: An index-based loop is useful here because the matching list element must be replaced in place.
The stable transaction id identifies the exact entry to update even when other values have changed.

lines.code: transactions.set(i, new Transaction(id, date, type, categoryName, amount, description));
lines.text: Replacing the object keeps the repository list consistent with the newly supplied transaction values.
Persisting after the loop makes the in-memory change durable in the application's data file.

phases: Apply the final update and delete behavior across repositories.
Wire editing controls and selection handling in each JavaFX view.
Run the complete test suite and open the finished application once.

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Project: PocketCFO App, Part 2
chapters.goal: Extend PocketCFO with CSV transaction imports, multi-month and year-to-date reporting, priority-versus-spending analysis, three-month category trends, and what-if reallocations to savings goals or obligations.

exercises.title: Import Transactions from CSV
exercises.description: Parse common bank-export column layouts, preserve valid rows when other rows fail, and connect CSV importing to the JavaFX interface.

explanation.summary: The Maven dependency adds Apache Commons CSV so PocketCFO can parse vendor exports without implementing fragile comma splitting itself.

lines.text: The group id identifies the organization that publishes the CSV library in Maven repositories.
The artifact id selects the Commons CSV component that understands quoted fields, headers, and row iteration.
Pinning a version makes dependency resolution repeatable instead of silently changing the project later.

explanation.run: Use the guided replay to materialize and test the PocketCFO project.

exercises.title: Create Sample Transaction Data
exercises.description: Create a representative CSV file for exercising PocketCFO's transaction importer.

explanation.summary: The sample file supplies the headers and signed transaction values expected by the CSV importer.

lines.text: The header names map each CSV column to the transaction field the importer should populate.
A positive amount represents incoming money and gives the importer an income example.
A negative amount represents spending and retains the category supplied by the export.

explanation.run: Use the guided replay to materialize and test the PocketCFO project.

exercises.title: Add Multi-Month and Year-to-Date Support
exercises.description: Navigate between months and calculate year-to-date category and summary totals.

explanation.summary: The year-to-date category total keeps the category, accumulated spending, scaled target, and income-only state together for reporting.

lines.text: Keeping the Category object lets the summary retain its name and target information without duplicating those fields.
The actual value stores the accumulated year-to-date amount using precise decimal arithmetic.
The target is scaled to the number of included months so actual spending is compared with an equivalent period.
This flag lets later reporting distinguish income categories from expense categories.

explanation.run: Use the guided replay to materialize and test the PocketCFO project.

exercises.title: Compare Spending with Category Priorities
exercises.description: Rank chosen category priorities beside categories ordered by actual spending to reveal alignment or mismatch.

explanation.summary: Categories can carry an optional numeric priority while remaining compatible with existing categories that have no assigned rank.

lines.text: Using the nullable Integer wrapper allows a category to remain unprioritized instead of inventing a numeric placeholder.
The original two-argument constructor delegates to the new constructor, preserving existing call sites.
Optional makes callers handle the absence of a priority explicitly before sorting or displaying it.
ofNullable converts the stored wrapper into either a present priority value or an empty Optional.

exercises.title: Visualize Three-Month Category Trends
exercises.description: Show selected spending categories across the selected month and two preceding months with compact text trends.

explanation.summary: The nested trend types pair each month with a precise spending amount and group three ordered points with the category they describe.

lines.text: The record keeps the month and its BigDecimal amount together as one immutable trend point.
Each trend retains the Category so the interface can label and select it without duplicating category data.
List.of stores the supplied monthly points in an immutable, oldest-to-newest sequence.
The getter exposes the ordered three-month history for formatting and comparison.

exercises.title: Preview Budget Reallocations
exercises.description: Preview reducing a category's monthly target and redirecting the amount to a savings goal or recurring obligation without changing stored data.

explanation.summary: The projection captures both sides of a previewed transfer so the interface can compare a reduced category target with improved goal or obligation progress.

lines.text: The proposed reduction is retained as the amount redirected from the category budget.
The original monthly target provides the baseline for the what-if comparison.
The new target shows the category budget after subtracting the proposed reduction.
The target kind distinguishes a savings goal from a recurring obligation while sharing one projection type.
The projected allocation adds the redirected amount to what has already been saved or paid.
The printed listing elides routine construction and accessors, while the replay scaffold retains the complete class.
